noTracking.body: There is no analytics, no advertising and no tracking pixel in openplate. Nothing you do in the app is counted, and nothing about it is sent anywhere.

selfHost.body: One stateless container, no database to run and no secret to configure. The compose file is in the repository, and the whole thing is a download and one command.

source.body: Read every line before you trust it with a day of your eating. Fork it, change it, ship it in something of your own — the licence asks for the copyright notice and nothing else.

connect.body: One click connects OpenRouter: you approve it there, and the key comes back to this device and stays on it. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works too. Reading a plate typically costs well under a cent per photo, and your provider bills you directly. Skip this and search still works — a key is only needed to read a photo.

sync.body: Log lunch on your phone, then look at the week on your laptop. Sync is opt-in and end-to-end encrypted: the ciphertext sits on an openplate-sync server — ours, or one you run yourself — and that server has no key to it, because the key is made from a passphrase it never sees.

research.title: Research contributions
research.intro: Studies you contribute to, what each one receives, and how to leave.
research.unavailable: This sync server has no research lane. Nothing can be sent or withdrawn here.
research.needsSession: Research contributions need your sync passphrase. Unlock sync on this device first.
research.loadFailed: Your studies could not be loaded.

caveats.pseudonymised: What a study receives is pseudonymised, never your name: it sees one stable pseudonym for you and your daily totals.
caveats.auxiliaryJoin: A stable pseudonym is not the same as being unidentifiable. Anyone holding another dataset about the same people may be able to re-identify you by joining it to this one.
caveats.unknownMacro: A macro that was unknown for an entry adds nothing to that day’s total, so a low total can mean unknown rather than little eaten. The study is told to read the entry count beside every total.

enrolments.title: Studies you contribute to
enrolments.empty: You are not contributing to a study. Joining one needs a fingerprint printed in its consent materials.
enrolments.window: Whole calendar days inside the window you send — one row per day, and never a time, a food name or a photo.
enrolments.sentWindow: Sent {{from}} to {{to}} — whole calendar days, one row per day, and never a time, a food name or a photo.
enrolments.fields: Each day carries energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat, fibre, and how many entries that day held.
enrolments.neverSent: Nothing has been sent to this study yet.
enrolments.pseudonymHint: This is what the study sees of you. Quote it if you ask a researcher to confirm your withdrawal was honoured.
enrolments.pseudonymUnknown: This device cannot work out your pseudonym — its research key is missing.

withdrawal.instructedToDelete: The study is instructed to delete your contribution, and openplate’s study tools drop it on every pull.
withdrawal.alreadyDownloaded: A copy the study already downloaded cannot be taken back — honouring the instruction is an obligation this system states and cannot enforce.
withdrawal.noNewData: No new data will be sent to this study.
withdrawal.samePseudonymOnRejoin: Leaving does not give you a new identity. If you join this study again you present the same pseudonym, so anyone who kept an old copy could link the two.
withdrawal.rejoinNeedsCeremony: This device forgets the study, so joining again means typing its fingerprint from the consent materials once more.
withdrawal.done: Withdrawn. The study is instructed to delete what it holds.
withdrawal.failed: The withdrawal did not go through. You are still contributing, so you can try again.
withdrawal.unavailable: This server has no research lane, so nothing was withdrawn. You are still contributing here.

export.pseudonymisedNotice: This data is PSEUDONYMISED, not anonymous: each participant is a stable pseudonym rather than a name, and anyone holding a second dataset about the same people may be able to re-identify them by joining on it.
export.withdrawn: Withdrawn and purged before this export: {{withdrawn}}. Their rows are not in this file and must not be recovered from an earlier one.
export.unopenable: Sealed to a key this device does not hold: {{unopenable}} of {{total}} contributions. They are not in this file. This is a key problem, not a data problem.
export.malformed: Not readable by this version: {{malformed}} contributions. A non-zero number here is a bug worth reporting.
export.unknownMacroCaveat: A macro that was unknown for an entry contributes nothing to that day total, so a low total may mean unknown rather than low intake. Read loggedEntryCount alongside every total, and treat a zero total with a non-zero count as unquantified.

anomaly.serverRetainedWithdrawn: WARNING FOR THE OPERATOR: this server handed over {{retained}} contribution(s) it had already been instructed to delete. They were purged here, and this deployment needs investigating.

join.title: Join a study
join.description: A study sent you a link. Joining it needs the fingerprint printed in its consent materials.
join.failed: Joining did not go through. Nothing was saved, so you can try again.
join.mismatch: That is not this key’s fingerprint. Nothing was saved. Check the characters in the consent materials and type them again.

claimed.unnamed: The link does not say which study this is.
claimed.unverified: Anyone who can write the link can write that name. What proves it is the study is the fingerprint below.

join.labelHint: Only for you, on this device. The study never sees it.
join.fingerprintHint: Type the twelve characters printed in the study’s consent materials. Do not take them off this screen or out of the link.
join.fingerprintWhy: The link brought the key; the printed page proves the key belongs to this study. Two separate ways of reaching you, and that is what makes the check worth anything.

enrolled.title: You have joined.
enrolled.body: Nothing has been sent yet. You choose which days go, and when, on your studies page.

setup.body: This step is entirely optional — logging by hand, and everything else in openplate, works fully without it. It needs a paid account with an AI service that you set up yourself (openplate doesn't run its own AI or offer a trial) — usually a couple of minutes to set up, and usually well under a cent per photo, billed by that provider, not by openplate. Once connected, each photo goes straight to your chosen provider to be read, then stays only on this device — never on openplate's server — until you clear it in Settings.
setup.bodyPreset: This step is entirely optional — logging by hand, and everything else in openplate, works fully without it. On this openplate you can connect its own AI in one tap, with no account and no key of your own. Once connected, each photo goes straight from this device to that AI to be read, then stays only on this device — never on openplate.org, and never anywhere else — until you clear it in Settings.

explainer.byok: Still interested? Here's the deal: openplate doesn't run its own AI, so it can't offer free photo scans. Instead you bring your own key from an AI company, and openplate uses it to read your plate photos — your key, your provider, your data. The key lives only on this device: openplate never sends it anywhere but the provider you choose below, and never stores or sees it on its own server.
explainer.notRequired: Nothing on this page is required. Your diary, goals, and trends all work without it. If signing up for a paid AI service and pasting in a key isn't for you, close this page and keep logging by hand — you lose nothing else.
explainer.photosAndCost: Each photo is sent straight to that provider just long enough to read your plate. openplate itself never keeps a copy on its own server — but by default it does keep a copy on this device afterward (in your browser's storage) for about 90 days, so you can see it again on that entry later. You can turn that off, or clear it anytime, under Data & backup in settings. It costs money, but not much: usually under a cent a photo, billed straight to you by your provider — even scanning every meal, most people spend well under $5 a month. You only pay for what you actually scan.
explainer.setup: Setup means visiting the provider's own site first: create a free account there, and add a payment method (their checkout, not ours — openplate never sees your card). The simplest path is a key from <providerLink>{{provider}}</providerLink> — that's the tab we've put first below, and one key covers every model listed under it.
explainer.setupOpenAiNote: One exception worth knowing: OpenAI's own service won't answer requests sent straight from a browser, so OpenAI models are only reachable here through OpenRouter — whose single key also covers Google's models.
explainer.title: Snap a photo, get the macros
